approvedWording: Live v7 passed standard desktop Chrome zoom spot checks at 200% and 400% across the four loaded sections. The blank job-link dialog scrolled its focused Save button into view and closed with Escape. Zoom was restored to 100%. Independent browser font preferences and broader accessibility and account acceptance remain open.
findings: The receipt labels the outcome as bounded zoom, navigation and blank-dialog checks rather than a complete accessibility audit.
The receipt records equal document client and scroll widths for all eight section/zoom observations, with no horizontal overflow in the checked visible element types.
The 400% section screenshot visibly contains the four navigation controls.
The 400% dialog screenshot visibly contains a focused, readable Save on this phone button.
The partially visible Search heading in the short viewport does not independently demonstrate clipping or unreachability.
Both JPEG byte lengths and SHA-256 hashes match the receipt.
limits: This review checked the saved receipt and two screenshots; it did not independently rerun the browser interactions.
The screenshots use CSS viewport resolution and do not display the browser zoom badge. The zoom setting is supported by the receipt of a separate native browser observation and DOM metrics.
Both saved screenshots show 400% states. The 200% observations and the other section states are recorded in the receipt, not separately visible in these two images.
The evidence concerns the four currently loaded section states and one blank job-link dialog, not every content state, control or keyboard traversal.
No WCAG conformance, full screen-reader acceptance, physical-device acceptance, mobile-browser zoom acceptance or multi-account/provider lifecycle acceptance is established.

Independent browser default-font preferences were not verified. The separate headless attempt failed before browser launch with a socket permission error; it is not a passing test and no bypass was attempted.
